owner: CC (code+proofs). No design ruling is owed yet — the shape question below is a corpus question, not Akien's.
intention: A WRITE-SCAN: given a directory, name every module that can write into it. The mirror of cairn/import_sieve for the other verb — `open(path,'w'|'a')`, `write_text`, `write_bytes`, `os.replace`, `shutil.copy*`, `subprocess` running a writing command — so Law 6's 'exactly one owner gates writes' can be measured on a directory the way sole-path is now measured on a port.
why:
IT WAS BORN AS A MISREADING, AND THAT IS THE POINT. intentions_model_compiler's filed edge (c) has read, since it was written, 'Law-6 single-writer is an IOU enforced by convention until the tester import-scans for a second writer of intentions-congruency-lab/'. On 2026-08-06 the import-scan was built, and it does not serve that sentence and never will: a module can write that directory while importing nothing unusual at all. The IOU had been parked behind an instrument that was never going to arrive — so it read as scheduled when it was actually homeless, which is worse than reading as open. Four of the five import-scan customers were closed that day; this is the fifth, and the honest version of it needs a different verb.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM. Someone re-runs the compiler and their hand-fixed line in intentions-congruency-lab/ is gone. They fix it again, in the compiled view again, because nothing on disk tells them the view is compiled — the charter says so, and the charter is the thing they were trying to edit. Today the only defence is that CC knows better, which is a discipline living in one agent's habit, i.e. exactly what Law 4 calls a debt.
traces_to: Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner; the owner alone gates writes — this measures whether that is true of a directory rather than asserting it)
Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — and an IOU pointed at the wrong instrument is a debt that looks like a plan)
Law 1 (the import-scan's graph-over-the-tree shape is already proven at cairn/import_sieve; this is a second verb over the same walk, not a second walk)
watchme: none, because it rests at THINKME and its whole open question is how coarse the mesh should be — a watch armed before that is answered would be counting occurrences of a predicate nobody has chosen yet. The watch question is answered when it is cast forward; the candidate is a count of modules the (a)-mesh names, which is the number that says whether the coarse answer is readable or noise.
gates: proof gate beside the code, under the tester. PAIRED TEETH, as import_sieve's are: every catching tooth shaken over a planted graph (must catch) and over the real corpus (must not), because a scanner that catches nothing reports the identical green as a clean corpus. And the mesh lesson carries over unchanged — a docstring naming a path is not a write, and a path in a fixture string is data.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a mention becomes a write — prose or a fixture naming the directory is reported as writing it; (2) a real writer escapes — a module that writes the target and is not named; (3) a clean result is returned over a tree the scan did not read (import_sieve's HollowScan, or this is not proven-space); (4) the scan reports a green that the corpus can trivially defeat WITHOUT that limit being written down (see the open question — a partial answer stated as partial is fine, a partial answer stated as complete is the defect).
the_open_question_and_it_is_the_whole_bu: HOW FAR DOES STATIC ANALYSIS GET, AND WHERE IS THE HONEST LINE? An import is a literal in the source; a write is a call whose target is usually a variable. `p.write_text(x)` where `p` came from a function argument is invisible to any scan that does not do dataflow, and Cairn is not building a dataflow engine. So the real question is not 'can we detect writers' but 'what is the smallest predicate that is both cheap and worth trusting'. Three candidates, cheapest first, and the answer is probably the first one: (a) WHO CAN NAME THE DIRECTORY AT ALL — any module containing the literal 'intentions-congruency-lab' outside a docstring is a candidate writer, no call analysis, deliberately over-broad, and the allowlist is short enough to read; (b) who names it AND calls a writing verb anywhere in the same module; (c) real dataflow, which is a research project and should be refused unless (a) and (b) measurably fail. Under Cairn's own build-minimal rule this ships as (a) with its coarseness stated in the charter, and grows only against a real miss. IMPORTANT: (a) is a coarser mesh than import_sieve's, and that is allowed as long as it is DECLARED — the sin is a green read wider than it is measured, not a mesh with a known size.
horizon: re-read when: a second directory wants single-writer enforcement (one customer is a case, two is a shape — until then this may be a check that belongs to intentions_model_compiler rather than a component of its own); or when a hand-edit of the compiled view actually happens, which turns the lived symptom from a prediction into a measurement.
provenance: Cast 2026-08-06 immediately after cairn/import_sieve was built at Akien's direction ('then it sounds like we do import-scan next'). Filed the same hour the misreading was found, because CLAUDE.md's own rule says an IOU without a real ticket is itself the defect that section is made of — and retiring four IOUs while leaving the fifth pointing at an instrument that cannot serve it would have been the same defect with better paperwork.
